title: Minimalist chrome — one look for every button

steps.path: Header buttons, quick buttons and status buttons
steps.headline: Which strength should every floating button share — header, quick buttons and status buttons alike?
steps.notice: Each picture is two separate views of the same screen: the top of the window (header over the wallpaper), a white gap, then the bottom (quick buttons, message box, status buttons). The message box itself is unchanged. The bottom buttons borrow the header's pale text so they stay readable.
steps.risk: With that pale text, the orange "Sonnet" label loses its orange. The "Priority" button keeps its own solid colour in all three (it would need its own change).

variants.label: Today, for comparison
variants.summary: Header buttons nearly clear; quick and status buttons much more solid. Two different looks.

variants.label: Close to the header
variants.summary: Every button is a faint frosted pill with a hairline edge. The most wallpaper shows through.
variants.risk: On a busy wallpaper patch the buttons' shapes are the hardest to make out.

variants.label: The midpoint
variants.summary: A little more fill and a clearer edge. Header icons gain a visible pill; the bottom buttons lose most of their solid look.

variants.label: Close to the chips
variants.summary: The most defined pills; header icons become obvious buttons.
variants.risk: The header starts to look busier: eleven pills in a row.
